title: Lonely runner conjecture
formal:
For every integer \(k\ge1\) and all distinct positive integers \(v_1,\ldots,v_k\), does there exist a real number \(t\ge0\) such that
\[\min_{1\le i\le k}\|tv_i\|_{\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}\ge\frac1{k+1}?\]
definitions: Here \(\|x\|_{\mathbb R/\mathbb Z}=\min_{m\in\mathbb Z}|x-m|\) is distance to the nearest integer. Think of k runners of speeds v_i starting with a stationary observer on a circle of circumference one. The formula asks for a time when every moving runner is at least 1/(k+1) away from that observer around the circle. The number of runners and speeds are unrestricted; no time bound is required.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof or refutation of the stated proposition, with all its quantifiers and hypotheses. Verification of finitely many parameter values does not establish the universal assertion.
why: A simultaneous separation question linking number theory, discrete geometry and graph coloring.

context_blocks.text: The survey explains the integer-speed formulation and connections to covering radii and distance-graph coloring.
The 2026 paper on lonely-runner relations restricts where counterexamples could lie, while retaining the conjecture for arbitrary numbers of runners.
